correctness.rationale: Independent exhaustive integer replay: /workspace/replay_5.py (Python 3 and SymPy) enumerates vertex-disjoint directed path covers, including singleton vertices, by recursively taking the component containing the least unused vertex. This enumerates each multipath exactly once without the frozen incidence-mask predicate or Morse matching. The augmented face counts are 1,16,80,144,72. The full signed deletion boundaries in levels 0 through 3 multiply consecutively to zero and have nonzero Smith factors 1; fifteen units; sixty-five units; seventy-one units and one 2, respectively. The kernel of the next outgoing map is primitive, so the incoming Smith factors give the homology torsion; the ranks give free rank 7 only in degree 2. This is Z^7 plus Z/2 there and no other reduced integral homology, not merely a field-rank check. Under Definitions 4.1–4.4 of arXiv:2208.04656v1, an edgeful region must contain any oriented cycle to which a selected edge belongs, in particular its opposite-edge digon. Every vertex of a connected edgeful region is consequently unstable within it. Every proper such subgraph of this connected graph shares a vertex with an omitted edge, violating boundary stability. The full graph satisfies the conditions vacuously on the boundary and is unstable at every vertex, so it is its own unique dynamical module. This contradicts the precise introduction conjecture of v1; no claim depends on whether the inaccessible journal version retained that wording.

value.rationale: As a mathematical result this is a well-motivated structural counterexample to a definite conjecture: a small canonical bidirected graph realizes integral torsion while all its vertices are unstable in its sole module. Specifying the integral group rather than only field Betti numbers makes the obstruction precise. Its intrinsic value does not make this already-covered record a distinct contribution.
